**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination — denial dated August 18, 2026**
- **Member name:** Quinn Lawson
- **Member ID:** W507278968
- **Reference number:** POC-4FAE25DEAC-53449
- **Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
- **Plan:** Blue Shield of California (Commercial/ACA), State of California
- **Governing policy:** *Partial Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears and Acromioplasty/Subacromial Decompression (BSC7.14)*, effective 7/1/2026 — https://www.blueshieldca.com/content/dam/bsca/en/provider/docs/medical-policies/Partial-Thickness-Rotator-Cuff-Tears-Acromioplasty-Subacromial-Decompression.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the prior authorization request for my shoulder surgery, rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827). The notice dated August 18, 2026 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Blue Shield of California to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I believe the records already in your file match the plan's own written criteria.

Below, I have set out the plan's criteria from the policy named above in the plan's own words, and then what my records show for each one. All policy language in quotation marks is copied from that policy.

---

### 1. The imaging criterion — the stated reason for the denial

The plan's policy states:

> "C. Documentation, including formal radiological interpretation and detailed report of bony or soft tissue pathology or abnormality (e.g., ultrasound, CT scan, or MRI) that demonstrates rotator cuff pathology (Grade I I – see Policy Guidelines) that corresponds with the individual's symptoms and clinical findings."

My records establish this. An MRI of the shoulder was performed on July 14, 2026. The MRI report documents a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This is a formal radiological interpretation of soft tissue pathology of the rotator cuff, and it corresponds directly with my symptoms and my exam: I have had nine months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest, I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, I cannot sleep on the affected side, and my exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side with range of motion limited by pain.

I would also point out what the policy says about the situation where imaging does not support surgery:

> "In-office reports (ultrasound and x- rays) should include a comprehensive description of the radiographic findings. In rare instances where the imaging is normal and does not support the need for this procedure, the history, physical exam, and MD rationale need to clearly show why surgery is indicated on exception, including why another cause is less likely."

That exception pathway is written for cases where the imaging is normal. My imaging is not normal. It identifies a specific, measured structural tear.

The criterion above refers to "Grade I I – see Policy Guidelines." The Policy Guidelines section that defines that grading was not included in the material I received, so I cannot tell how it was applied to my MRI. I am asking the plan to identify the specific criterion and the specific grading definition it relied on when it concluded my imaging does not support the surgery, and to state how the MRI finding of a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy was evaluated against it. I note that the policy I was pointed to addresses partial thickness tears, while my MRI reports a full-thickness tear; if a different policy or criteria set governs a full-thickness tear, I ask that the plan identify it and review my request under the correct criteria.

The policy also lists the documentation the plan expects, including:

> "• Radiology reports (e.g., ultrasound, CT, MRI) used to make surgical decision • Documented exclusion of other possible causative conditions • Prior conservative treatments, duration, and response or reason conservative treatment is inappropriate"

and

> "• Past and present diagnostic testing and results • Pertinent past procedural and surgical history"

The MRI report of July 14, 2026 is the radiology study used to make the surgical decision. If any of these items is missing from the file the reviewer worked from, I ask that the plan tell me which one, so my surgeon's office can send it rather than have the request denied for a records gap.

---

### 2. Pain, weakness, and loss of function

The plan's policy states:

> "A. Individual has painful range of motion, documented loss of muscle strength of the rotator cuff musculature, or documented shoulder function disability, any of which significantly interferes with the ability to perform activities of daily living, duties of employment, athletic participation, or sleep"

My records establish this. My exam documents range of motion limited by pain. My records document that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. Sleep and overhead reaching are exactly the kinds of daily activities this criterion describes. This criterion is written so that any one of the listed findings satisfies it, and my records document more than one.

The policy also asks for:

> "• History and physical and/or consultation notes including: o Type of procedure o Reason for procedure o Clinical records indicating pain, loss of muscle strength of the rotator cuff musculature, and/or functional disability that interferes with ADLs"

My surgeon's records identify the procedure and the reason for it and document the pain and functional loss described above.

---

### 3. Positive orthopedic testing

The plan's policy states:

> "B. Documentation of a positive result of one or more of the following orthopedic tests when compared to the non-affected side (see Policy Guidelines): 1. Neer Impingement Test 2. Hawkins Kennedy Impingement Test 3. Painful Arc Test 4. Full/Empty Can Test"

and continues:

> "5. Pain or weakness with infraspinatus and supraspinatus maneuvers such as: a. External Lag Sign at 90 Degrees Test b. Infraspinatus Test c. Empty Can Test (or the similar Jobe's Test) 6. Liftoff/Modified Liftoff Test 7. Belly-Press Test 8. Drop Arm Test"

My records state that I had positive provocative testing on the affected side. The summary I have does not name each individual test, so I am not going to guess at names my chart may not use. I ask that the plan review my surgeon's examination note directly, and I have asked my surgeon's office to confirm in writing which of the named tests above were performed and positive: [insert the specific test names and results from Dr. Reyes' examination note, including the comparison to the non-affected side].

This criterion requires only "one or more" of the listed tests. If the plan considers this criterion unmet, I ask that it say so specifically rather than resting on the imaging.

---

### 4. Other possible causes of shoulder pain

The plan's policy states:

> "D. When present, other possible causative conditions of shoulder pain are documented to have been excluded, less likely, or mild in nature. These conditions may include but are not limited to glenohumeral arthritis, frozen shoulder/adhesive capsulitis, brachial plexus disorders, fracture, referred neck pain, and thoracic outlet syndrome."

My MRI identified a specific structural cause for my symptoms in the tendon itself — a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm — and that finding matches where my pain is and what I cannot do with my arm. To the extent the plan requires more on this point, I ask that my surgeon's assessment be reviewed, and my surgeon's office can supply: [insert Dr. Reyes' documentation addressing other possible causes of shoulder pain].

---

### 5. Conservative (non-surgical) treatment

The plan's policy states:

> "E. Documentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy for at least six weeks (non-surgical medical management, see Policy Guidelines), or documentation of rationale if conservative therapy is considered inappropriate"

and:

> "• Conservative treatment for at least six weeks is required except for injury caused by acute trauma or if pain precludes the individual from continuing with a conservative plan (e.g., physical therapy) and exacerbates symptoms"

and:

> "Note: Prior conservative treatment for at least six weeks is required except for injury caused by acute trauma needing urgent repair."

My records establish this, and well beyond the period the plan states. I completed supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics — 20 visits over 16 weeks, from March 8, 2026 to June 28, 2026. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. That is substantially more than the six weeks the plan's own language requires.

The policy further states:

> "As medically indicated, members with partial thickness rotator cuff tears should have non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record, including all of the following, unless contraindicated:"

> "• Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics • Activity modification using the arm at or above the shoulder level • Supervised physical therapy which could include an instructed home exercise program, including flexibility and muscle-strengthening exercises"

My records match these items. I took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief. I completed the supervised physical therapy described above, which included rotator cuff strengthening. As to activity modification with the arm at or above shoulder level, my records document that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height at all.

The policy adds:

> "• Therapeutic injections into the subacromial space in the shoulder as appropriate (recommended, but not required)"

Although the plan states injections are recommended but not required, I had one anyway: a corticosteroid injection on May 2, 2026, which gave only about four weeks of partial relief.

In short, I did the full course of non-surgical care, for far longer than the plan's stated minimum, and my pain has continued to progress over nine months without relief from rest.

---

### A note on what I have and have not quoted

I have quoted only language that appears in the policy excerpts available to me. Some of that language points to a "Policy Guidelines" section and to lists that were not reproduced in what I received, and the policy contains further conditions and definitions that I have not seen. Because of that, I have not tried to state or guess at any threshold, grade, or measurement as a plan requirement unless the plan's own quoted words state it. Where I could not verify the plan's standard, I have argued from what my medical records actually say.

I am asking the plan to identify, in writing, the exact criterion and the exact language it applied in reaching this denial, along with the credentials of the reviewer who made the decision.

---

### What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Blue Shield of California to:

1. Overturn the August 18, 2026 denial (reference POC-4FAE25DEAC-53449) and authorize rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827;
2. Have my appeal reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic shoulder surgery;
3. Review the complete record, including the MRI report of July 14, 2026, my surgeon's examination and consultation notes, and the physical therapy discharge note covering March 8, 2026 through June 28, 2026; and
4. If the denial is maintained, tell me in writing which specific criterion of *Partial Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears and Acromioplasty/Subacromial Decompression (BSC7.14)* was not met, what documentation would satisfy it, and what my further appeal rights are, including independent external review.

My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **February 14, 2027**. I am submitting this appeal within that period. I understand this appeal may be filed online using the member grievance form at blueshieldca.com (logging in pre-fills the form), by phone at 1-800-393-6130 (TTY 711), or by mail to Blue Shield of California, Attn: Member Services Grievances, P.O. Box 5588, El Dorado Hills, CA 95762-0011.

My shoulder pain has gotten worse over nine months, I cannot raise my arm overhead, and I cannot sleep on that side. I have done everything that was asked of me before surgery. I would be grateful for a careful second look at this decision.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Quinn Lawson**
